001package io.github.ai4ci.functions;
002
003import java.io.Serializable;
004import java.util.Arrays;
005
006import org.apache.commons.math3.analysis.integration.BaseAbstractUnivariateIntegrator;
007import org.apache.commons.math3.analysis.integration.RombergIntegrator;
008import org.immutables.value.Value;
009
010import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonIgnore;
011import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonTypeInfo;
012import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonTypeName;
013import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.annotation.JsonDeserialize;
014import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.annotation.JsonSerialize;
015
016import io.github.ai4ci.functions.Coordinates.DuplicateResolution;
017import io.github.ai4ci.util.Conversions;
018import io.github.ai4ci.util.Sampler;
019
020/**
021 * Empirical probability distribution constructed from sample data or from x /
022 * F(x) pairs.
023 *
024 * <p>
025 * Main purpose: provide cumulative, density, quantile and sampling
026 * functionality for empirically observed variables. The implementation fits a
027 * monotonic spline on a transformed scale and exposes convenient accessors for
028 * mean, median, density and random sampling.
029 *
030 * <p>
031 * Downstream uses: consumed by in-host configuration and calibration routines
032 * (for example {@link io.github.ai4ci.config.inhost.InHostConfiguration} and
033 * {@link io.github.ai4ci.abm.Calibration}) and by initialisers that need
034 * empirical sampling behaviour.
035 *
036 * @author Rob Challen
037 */
038@Value.Immutable
039@JsonSerialize(as = ImmutableEmpiricalDistribution.class)
040@JsonDeserialize(as = ImmutableEmpiricalDistribution.class)
041@JsonTypeInfo(use = JsonTypeInfo.Id.NAME)
042@JsonTypeName("empirical")
043public interface EmpiricalDistribution extends Distribution, Serializable {
044
045        /**
046         * Number of knots to use when fitting the spline. If the number of data
047         * points exceeds this value, the data will be downsampled to this number of
048         * points to ensure a smooth fit and to avoid overfitting. If the number of
049         * data points is less than or equal to this value, the data will be used as
050         * is without downsampling.
051         *
052         */
053        int KNOTS = 50;
054
055        /**
056         * Convenience factory that builds an empirical distribution from raw sample
057         * data using a default link function.
058         *
059         * @param data samples used to estimate the distribution
060         * @return an immutable empirical distribution fitted to the samples
061         */
062        static ImmutableEmpiricalDistribution fromData(double... data) {
063                return fromData(LinkFunction.NONE, data);
064        }
065
066        /**
067         * Construct an empirical distribution from sample data using the supplied
068         * link function for transformation prior to fitting.
069         *
070         * @param link the link function applied to the sample values prior to
071         *             fitting
072         * @param data the raw samples used to build the empirical distribution
073         * @return an immutable empirical distribution fitted to the samples
074         */
075        static ImmutableEmpiricalDistribution fromData(
076                        LinkFunction link, double... data
077        ) {
078
079                Arrays.sort(data);
080                var out = ImmutableEmpiricalDistribution.builder();
081
082                var meanH = Arrays.stream(data)
083                        .map(link::fn)
084                        .average()
085                        .getAsDouble();
086                var varH = Arrays.stream(data)
087                        .map(link::fn)
088                        .map(d -> Math.pow(d - meanH, 2))
089                        .average()
090                        .getAsDouble();
091
092                var min = link.invFn(meanH - 5 * Math.sqrt(varH));
093                var max = link.invFn(meanH + 5 * Math.sqrt(varH));
094
095                out.setMinimum(min);
096                out.setMaximum(max);
097
098                if (data.length > KNOTS) {
099
100                        var step = ((float) data.length) / KNOTS;
101                        var x = new double[KNOTS - 1];
102                        var y = new double[KNOTS - 1];
103                        for (var i = 1; i < KNOTS; i++) {
104                                double ix = i * step;
105                                var i0 = (int) Math.floor(ix);
106                                var i1 = (int) Math.ceil(ix);
107                                if (i0 == i1)
108                                        x[i - 1] = data[i0];
109                                else
110                                        x[i - 1] = data[i0] * (i1 - ix) + data[i1] * (ix - i0);
111                                y[i - 1] = ((double) i) / (KNOTS);
112                        }
113                        out.setX(x);
114                        out.setCumulativeProbability(y);
115                } else {
116                        // use the data as is
117                        var y = new double[data.length];
118                        for (var i = 0; i < data.length; i++)
119                                y[i] = (i + 1.0) / (data.length + 1.0);
120                        out.setX(data);
121                        out.setCumulativeProbability(y);
122                }
123                out.setLink(link);
124                return out.build();
125
126        }
127
128        /**
129         * Baseline an odds-like function to produce a probability distribution by
130         * scaling so that the product odds * density integrates to one.
131         *
132         * @param odds the odds-like empirical function to baseline against this
133         *             density
134         * @return a probability distribution function derived from the supplied odds
135         */
136        default EmpiricalFunction baselineOdds(EmpiricalFunction odds) {
137                var tmp = new RombergIntegrator(
138                                0.0001, 0.0001,
139                                BaseAbstractUnivariateIntegrator.DEFAULT_MIN_ITERATIONS_COUNT,
140                                RombergIntegrator.ROMBERG_MAX_ITERATIONS_COUNT
141                );
142                var total = tmp.integrate(
143                        100000,
144                        x -> odds.value(x) * this.getDensity(x),
145                        this.getMinimum(),
146                        this.getMaximum()
147//          Math.max(this.getMinimum(), odds.getMinimum()),
148//          Math.min(this.getMaximum(), odds.getMaximum())
149                );
150
151                return ImmutableEmpiricalFunction.builder()
152                        .setLink(this.getLink())
153                        .setX(odds.getX())
154                        .setY(
155                                Arrays.stream(odds.getY())
156                                        .map(y -> y / total)
157                                        .toArray()
158                        )
159                        .build();
160        }
161
162        /**
163         * Return the cumulative distribution value at the supplied x.
164         *
165         * @param x the point at which to evaluate the CDF
166         * @return the cumulative probability F(x) in the unit interval
167         */
168        @JsonIgnore
169        default double getCumulative(double x) {
170                return Conversions.expit(
171                        this.getLogitLinkCDF()
172                                .interpolate(
173                                        this.getLink()
174                                                .fn(x)
175                                )
176                );
177        }
178
179        /**
180         * The cumulative probabilities corresponding to {@link #getX()}.
181         *
182         * @return an array of cumulative probabilities in the unit interval
183         */
184        double[] getCumulativeProbability();
185
186        /**
187         * Compute the density at the supplied x using the derivative of the fitted
188         * spline and the link function.
189         *
190         * @param x the point at which to evaluate the density
191         * @return the density f(x) at the point x
192         */
193        @JsonIgnore
194        default double getDensity(double x) {
195
196                if ((this.getMinimum() >= x) || (this.getMaximum() <= x)
197                                || !this.getLink()
198                                        .inSupport(x))
199                        return 0;
200
201                // density is differential of the function:
202                // expit(spline(link(x)))
203                // = expit'(spline(link(x))) * spline'(link(x)) * link'(x))
204
205                return
206                // expit'(spline(link(x))
207                LinkFunction.LOGIT.derivInvFn(
208                        this.getLogitLinkCDF()
209                                .interpolate(
210                                        this.getLink()
211                                                .fn(x)
212                                )
213                ) *
214                // spline'(link(x))
215                                this.getLogitLinkCDF()
216                                        .differential(
217                                                this.getLink()
218                                                        .fn(x)
219                                        )
220                                *
221                                // link'(x)
222                                this.getLink()
223                                        .derivFn(x);
224        }
225
226        /**
227         * The link function applied to the domain when fitting the spline.
228         *
229         * @return the link function used for fitting and inversion
230         */
231        @Override @Value.Default
232        default LinkFunction getLink() { return LinkFunction.NONE; }
233
234        /**
235         * The quantile function is the inverse of the CDF. By fitting the spline on
236         * the logit-transformed cumulative probabilities, we can easily derive the
237         * quantile function by inverting the spline and applying the inverse link
238         * function.
239         *
240         * @return a spline interpolator representing the quantile function
241         */
242        @JsonIgnore @Value.Lazy
243        default SplineInterpolator getLinkLogitQuantile() {
244                return this.getLogitLinkCDF()
245                        .generateInverse();
246        }
247
248        /**
249         * The spline is fitted on the transformed scale to ensure monotonicity and
250         * to allow for flexible support. The link function transforms the x values
251         * to a scale suitable for fitting, while the logit transformation of the
252         * cumulative probabilities ensures that the fitted function can capture
253         * probabilities in the unit interval without boundary issues.
254         *
255         * @return a spline interpolator representing logit(F(X)) as a function of
256         *         link(X)
257         */
258        @JsonIgnore @Value.Derived
259        default SplineInterpolator getLogitLinkCDF() {
260                Coordinates tmp = ImmutableCoordinates.builder()
261                        .setX(this.getX())
262                        .setY(this.getCumulativeProbability())
263                        .setXLink(this.getLink())
264                        .setYLink(LinkFunction.LOGIT)
265                        .setIncreasing(true)
266                        .setResolveDuplicates(DuplicateResolution.MAX)
267                        .setXMin(this.getMinimum())
268                        .setXMax(this.getMaximum())
269                        .build();
270                return SplineInterpolator
271                        .createMonotoneCubicSpline(tmp.getHx(), tmp.getHy());
272        }
273
274        /**
275         * Maximum support value for the distribution.
276         *
277         * @return the maximum domain value for which the distribution is defined
278         */
279        double getMaximum();
280
281        /**
282         * Maximum support used internally by derived methods. This mirrors
283         * {@link #getMaximum()} and is provided for clarity in templates.
284         *
285         * @return the upper support bound
286         */
287        @Override @Value.Derived @JsonIgnore
288        default double getMaxSupport() { return this.getMaximum(); }
289
290        /**
291         * Compute the mean of the distribution using numerical integration.
292         *
293         * @return the expected value (mean) of the distribution
294         */
295        @JsonIgnore @Value.Lazy
296        default double getMean() {
297                var tmp = new RombergIntegrator(
298                                0.001, 0.001,
299                                BaseAbstractUnivariateIntegrator.DEFAULT_MIN_ITERATIONS_COUNT,
300                                RombergIntegrator.ROMBERG_MAX_ITERATIONS_COUNT
301                );
302                return tmp.integrate(
303                        100000,
304                        x -> x * this.getDensity(x),
305                        this.getMinimum(),
306                        this.getMaximum()
307                );
308        }
309
310        /**
311         * Convenience accessor for the median.
312         *
313         * @return the 0.5 quantile (median)
314         */
315        @JsonIgnore
316        default double getMedian() { return this.getQuantile(0.5); }
317
318        /**
319         * Minimum support value for the distribution.
320         *
321         * @return the minimum domain value for which the distribution is defined
322         */
323        double getMinimum();
324
325        /**
326         * Minimum support used internally by derived methods. This mirrors
327         * {@link #getMinimum()} and is provided for clarity in templates.
328         *
329         * @return the lower support bound
330         */
331        @Override @Value.Derived @JsonIgnore
332        default double getMinSupport() { return this.getMinimum(); }
333
334        /**
335         * Return the p-th quantile of the distribution.
336         *
337         * @param p a probability in [0,1]
338         * @return the quantile corresponding to p
339         */
340        @JsonIgnore
341        default double getQuantile(double p) {
342                return this.getLink()
343                        .invFn(
344                                this.getLinkLogitQuantile()
345                                        .interpolate(LinkFunction.LOGIT.fn(p))
346                        );
347        }
348
349        /**
350         * The x coordinates used to construct the empirical cumulative.
351         *
352         * @return an array of x values (in ascending order) used for the CDF
353         */
354        double[] getX();
355
356        /**
357         * Sample a random value from the empirical distribution using the default
358         * sampler.
359         *
360         * @return a random draw from the distribution
361         */
362        @Override @JsonIgnore
363        default double sample() {
364                var rng = Sampler.getSampler();
365                return this.sample(rng);
366        }
367
368        /**
369         * Sample a random value using the supplied {@link Sampler} instance.
370         *
371         * @param rng the random number generator to use
372         * @return a random draw from the distribution
373         */
374        @Override @JsonIgnore
375        default double sample(Sampler rng) {
376                return this.getLink()
377                        .invFn(
378                                this.getLinkLogitQuantile()
379                                        .interpolate(LinkFunction.LOGIT.fn(rng.nextDouble()))
380                        );
381        }
382}
